page_01: One of the first cupcake recipes, from 1796, said to bake the cake in small cups!
page_02: People have been making pancakes for thousands of years!
page_03: Honey can stay good to eat for thousands of years!
page_04: A strawberry has about 200 tiny seeds on the outside!
page_05: Vanilla ice cream gets its flavor from the seed pods of an orchid flower!
page_06: Popcorn pops when a tiny drop of water inside each kernel turns to steam!
page_07: Pizza comes from Naples in Italy, where people have baked it for hundreds of years.
page_08: Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not!
page_09: A watermelon is about 92 percent water. That's why it's so juicy!
page_10: The first carrots were purple and yellow, not orange!
page_11: Apples float in water because about one quarter of an apple is air!
page_12: A pineapple plant takes about two years to grow one pineapple!
page_13: Peanuts aren't really nuts. They grow underground, like beans!
page_14: Chocolate is made from cacao beans that grow in big pods on cacao trees!
page_15: A dentist helped invent the cotton candy machine more than 100 years ago!
page_16: An 11-year-old boy invented the ice pop after leaving his drink outside on a cold night!
page_18: Rice is the main food for more than half of all the people in the world!
page_19: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of rows!
page_20: Blueberries are one of the very few foods that are naturally blue!
page_21: A lemon tree can grow flowers and lemons all year long!
page_22: Raisins are grapes that have been dried in the sun!
page_23: Broccoli is a flower! Each little bump is a tiny flower bud.
page_24: Potatoes were the first vegetable ever grown in space!
page_25: An avocado is a fruit, and each one has one big seed inside!
page_26: Tomatoes are fruit, because they grow from a flower and hold seeds!
page_27: A pumpkin is a fruit, and it can have hundreds of seeds inside!
page_28: Coconuts can float across the ocean and grow on a faraway beach!
page_29: Chocolate chip cookies were first baked in Massachusetts in the 1930s!
page_30: The hole in a donut helps it cook evenly all the way through!
page_31: Some say a pretzel's twisty shape looks like arms folded across a chest!
page_32: Yeast makes bread dough rise by filling it with tiny bubbles of gas!
page_33: The first American waffle iron was invented in 1869!
page_34: The first marshmallows were made from a plant called the marsh mallow!
page_35: A dairy cow can make more than 6 gallons of milk in one day!
page_36: Sandwiches are named after the Earl of Sandwich, a man from England!
page_37: Cinnamon comes from the bark of a tree!
page_38: The kiwifruit is named after the kiwi bird of New Zealand!
page_39: Tea is the most popular drink in the world, after water!
page_40: S'mores got their name because everyone wants some more!
page_41: People have put candles on birthday cakes for hundreds of years!
page_42: The holes in Swiss cheese come from tiny bubbles of gas!
page_43: It takes about 40 gallons of tree sap to make 1 gallon of maple syrup!
page_44: Some bamboo can grow about 3 feet in just one day!
page_45: A navel orange has a tiny second orange growing at its bottom end!
page_46: There are more than 7,500 kinds of apples in the world!
page_47: A hen can lay almost one egg every day!
page_48: Mangoes are cousins of cashews and pistachios!
page_49: Cranberries have tiny pockets of air inside, so they float and even bounce!
page_50: Thanks for coloring with the Yummy Cuties. Enjoy a tasty treat!
